problem: The text says y, the test statistic, is 'in volts'. It cannot be: r(t) is in volts and the reference waveform √(2/Tb)cos(2πfct) has units of 1/√s, so the integral carries units of V·√s (equivalently √joules with a 1 Ω reference). A student who checks dimensions will be confused, and the same symbol y is later compared against zero as if it were a voltage.
fix: Drop the unit word, or say: y is the test statistic, in units of √joules (V·√s) for a 1 Ω reference; its scale is set by the correlator normalisation √(2/Tb), which makes the signal part equal to ±√Eb.

problem: With rectangular (NRZ) pulses the power spectral density of BPSK is sinc-squared shaped, not sinc shaped; the sinc shape describes the amplitude spectrum. Saying 'sinc-shaped band' can leave a student with the wrong picture of the PSD.
fix: With rectangular pulses the BPSK power spectral density is proportional to sinc²((f − fc)Rb) around fc, with nulls at fc ± Rb, so the null-to-null bandwidth is 2Rb.

problem: The noise term n is introduced but its statistics are never given, although every later result (the Q(·) expression) depends on them. A student cannot see where N0/2 enters the argument.
fix: Add one line: n is Gaussian with mean zero and variance N0/2, so y is Gaussian with mean ±√Eb and variance N0/2, which gives Pb = Q(√(2Eb/N0)).
